text.p: Ceramic tile maker Dal-Tile International said Wednesday it foresaw improved performance in the second half of the year as it finished merging with a company it had acquired last year.
Dal-Tile said it and American Olean were about to integrate their management information systems after overcoming a number of delays.
"Migration of the sales centers, plants and regional distribution centers to the new system is progressing in accordance with the company's revised expectations," it said.

"Steady progress on this front, continued strength in construction activity and the planned addition of 58 million square feet of tile-making capacity in 1997 at an installed cost well below the industry average should contribute to improved performance in the second half of 1997," it added.
A spokeswoman for the company said Dal-Tile saw construction activity in residential and commercial buildings.
Dal-Tile reported first quarter earnings of $0.12 a share against $0.02 for the same period a year ago. The prior-year figure included a special charge of $0.12 a share.

First Call's consensus among analysts forecasts a profit of $0.21 a share for the second quarter against $0.17 the previous year, $0.33 for the third quarter against $0.27 and $0.36 for the fourth quarter against $0.28.
